findings.title: Provider now forces auto-memory off for any caller that leaves `setting_sources` unset
findings.description: `create_agent` now calls `sdk_settings_options(config.setting_sources or [], auto_memory=config.auto_memory, ...)` and always writes `kwargs["env"]`. `AgentConfig.auto_memory` defaults to `False`. Any caller that leaves both fields at their defaults, such as `sq serve` agents, now silently gets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`. Previously the variable was set only when `setting_sources == []`. The diff comments say "sq serve callers may pass None", and `describe_setting_sources` adds a "cli default" label for them (D10). Auto-memory for those callers has still changed from CLI default to off, and nothing records that. Either keep the old conditional for the `None` case or document the change and test it. `TestAutoMemory` only covers `setting_sources=["project"]`.

findings.title: Wait loop and idle-timeout path ship without a load or latency test
findings.description: The project's Python rules require a load test for code on concurrency or event-loop paths. `dispatch` now has a per-message `asyncio.timeout`, a stream re-read loop and `stop_task` cleanup. The new tests use `ScriptedClient` with small sleeps (0.05–0.15 s). They show the logic works but don't assert bounds on latency or resource use. This is worth adding, but it shouldn't block the change.

findings.title: `TimeoutError` handler in the wait loop can mistake other timeouts for idle expiry
findings.description: While background agents are running, `_collect_turns` catches any `TimeoutError` from `_read_turn_with_retry` and treats it as an idle timeout. It stops the agents and returns the partial text. If the SDK or CLI client raises its own `TimeoutError` inside `receive_response()`, the handler also swallows that. The warning then says "no activity for Ns", which would be misleading. Consider scoping the timeout, for example by checking that `asyncio.timeout(...).expired()` is true before treating it as an idle timeout. Let other `TimeoutError`s propagate.

findings.title: Type-suppression comments and `object`-typed test helpers weaken strict pyright
findings.description: `setting_sources=settings["setting_sources"]` needs `# pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]`, because `SdkSettings.setting_sources` is `list[str]` while the SDK expects a literal-typed list. `provider.py` also uses `# type: ignore[arg-type]` on `base_env`. In tests, `scripted_session`, `sdk_text`, `sdk_result` and `typed_config` all return `object`. This forces `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` at many call sites in `test_sdk_session.py`. Type `SdkSettings.setting_sources` with the SDK's `SettingSource` literal. Give the test helpers real return types: `SDKExecutionSession`, `AssistantMessage`, `ResultMessage` and a `Callable`. Strict pyright's no-errors rule would then hold without suppressions.

findings.title: Exception handling in the new session code follows project rules
findings.description: The broad `except Exception` in `_stop_background` has a `noqa: BLE001` and a comment explaining why no narrower type exists. It also logs with `logger.exception`. `_reconnect` logs and re-raises, and records `unusable_reason` so later calls fail fast through `_require_usable`. The stream-ended-with-agent-running case raises a `ProviderError`. All of these failure paths are observable and tested.

findings.title: `describe_system_prompt` docstring refers to a table that may not exist
findings.description: The `SystemPromptMode` docstring says "the four rows of the table above". The diff doesn't show a table above it, and I didn't confirm one exists. If there isn't one, the docstring should drop that reference.

findings.title: Bool config support is well covered
findings.description: The lenient bool parsing accepts several spellings, ignores case and whitespace, and raises an error that names the key. `get_typed_config` checks `bool` before `int`, with a comment explaining why. Parametrized tests and CLI round-trip tests cover this.
